# template_definitions-instructions_requests.md
Michael Brennan house standard for OUTBOUND discovery request sets. Client-clean by construction — merge fields in {{snake_case}}. Source: Michael's long-form request exemplars, adopted as the project standard 2026-08-11. The document structure this template lives inside: caption → cause no. → two-line bold title ("PLAINTIFF'S FIRST SET OF DISCOVERY REQUESTS TO / DEFENDANT {{defendant_name}}") → TO paragraph → Preamble (below) → signature block → certificate of service → **page break** → Definition of Terms (below, own pages) → confer note → **page break** → Interrogatories (own pages, "ANSWER:" prompt after each) → defendant Verification page → **page break** → Requests for Production (own pages, "RESPONSE:" prompt) → **page break** → Requests for Admissions (own pages, "ADMIT OR DENY:" prompt). Times New Roman 12 throughout; section headers centered bold underlined.

---

## Preamble (five paragraphs, follows the TO paragraph)

These requests are served pursuant to Rules 193, 196, 197, and 198 of the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure. Plaintiff requests that Defendant answer separately and fully in writing and under oath each of the following interrogatories within thirty (30) days after service of this request. For the attached requests for production, Plaintiff requests that the Defendant produce copies of, or permit Plaintiff to inspect, sample, test, photograph, and/or copy the designated documents, records, or tangible things which are in your possession, custody, or control, or are available to you, or are in the possession, custody, or control of your agents, representatives, or attorneys.

Plaintiff designates the manner of discovery to be by Defendant providing Plaintiff's attorney with a photocopy or duplicate of each of the designated documents, records, or tangible things in Defendant's possession, custody, or control, or by making the designated items available for inspection, sampling, testing, photographing and/or copying at the office of Plaintiff's attorney. If the requested documents, records, or tangible things cannot readily be copied, produced, and delivered to Plaintiff's attorneys, or made available for inspection, sampling, testing, photographing, and/or copying at the office of Plaintiff's attorney, Plaintiff is agreeable to conducting discovery in the office of Defendant's counsel or Defendant's premises or obtaining delivery therefrom. Plaintiff will return Defendant's photographs, movies, video tapes, and tangible unduplicated items to Defendant as requested by Defendant. {{optional_esi_sentence: Electronically stored information, including any {{case_specific_data_systems}}, is requested in its native format or another reasonably usable form pursuant to Rule 196.4 of the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure.}}

Plaintiff designates thirty (30) days after service of this request for discovery and inspection as the date to obtain custody of such items. Pursuant to RULE 193.5 of the TEXAS RULES OF CIVIL PROCEDURE, these Requests for Production and Discovery are continuing in nature and require supplementation as soon as is practical, but in no event less than thirty (30) days prior to the beginning of trial, and specifically include supplementation regarding expert witnesses, and expert witnesses' reports, physical models, compilations of data, photographs or videos, and other materials that have been prepared by, relied upon, reviewed by, or used by an expert.

For the attached requests for admissions, you are requested to admit or deny the truth of statements or opinions of fact or of the application of law to fact, including the genuineness of any documents served with this request or otherwise furnished or made available for inspection and copying. This request extends to all matters set forth in the accompanying attachments.

Each matter of which an admission is requested will be admitted unless, within thirty (30) days after service of this request, you serve upon the Plaintiff, through the undersigned attorney of record, a written answer or objection concerning such matter, either specifically denying the matter of which an admission is requested or setting forth in detail the reasons why you cannot truthfully either admit or deny the matter.

## Definition of Terms (numbered; starts on its own page after the certificate of service)

1. The terms "incident in question", "occurrence in question", or "occasion in question" mean and refer to any and all events which transpired on or about {{incident_date}}, {{optional_incident_location}}, and which are further described in Plaintiff's Original Petition or Plaintiff's last amended petition{{optional_crash_report_reference}}. {{optional_defined_term_bridge: The terms "the Incident" and "the incident in question," as used in these requests, have the same meaning.}}

2. "You" and "your" mean {{defendant_name}} and all agents, servants, employees, representatives, and/or other persons acting or purporting to act on its behalf or with its authority.

3. "Concerning" or "concern" mean referring to, alluding to, responding to, relating to, connected with, commenting on, in respect of, about, regarding, discussing, showing, describing, mentioning, reflecting, analyzing, constituting, evidencing, and pertaining to.

4. The terms "document" or "documents", as used herein, are to be construed as broadly as are the terms "writings and recordings" in Tex. R. Evid. 1001 and, without limitation, shall refer to the originals and all drafts and non-identical copies (whether different from the original by reason of notations made on such copies, or otherwise) of all letters, telegrams, memoranda, notes, records, diaries, charts, recordings, X-rays, work records, reports, studies, analysis, tabulations, graphs, logs, work sheets, specifications, photographs, videotapes, films, slides, negatives, contracts, telexes, fax and cable communications, summaries, files, desk files, surveys, receipts, notices, invoices, computer-stored data (disks) capable of being reduced to a document or documents, calendars, test reports, inspection reports, notes of conversations or communications, {{optional_esi_expansion: electronically stored information of every kind (including e-mail, text messages, databases, and metadata),}} and all other written or recorded information and materials of any nature whatsoever in the actual or constructive possession, custody, or control of {{defendant_name}} or any of its employees, agents, and/or any person or entity over whom you have control, and/or any person or entity as against whom you have a superior right to compel production.

5. The term "person", as used herein, means any natural person and, in addition, any firm, partnership, professional association, joint venture, corporation, trust, association, or other entity of any nature or character, including government agencies or entities of any kind, together with the partners, trustees, officers, directors, employees, or agents thereof.

6. "Identify" or "identity", when used in reference to a document, means to state the author's name and address, the date, title, and number of pages, the type of document (e.g., telefax, chart, medical record, etc.), and any other or further description that will permit proper designation for purposes of framing a request for production and inspection. In "identifying", it is not sufficient to only identify existing documents within your present possession, custody, or control. Where responsive to any of the following interrogatories, you must identify, to the fullest extent possible, any and all documents which you believe to have once existed, irrespective of that document's present existence, and regardless of whoever had or presently has possession, custody, or control of that document. In lieu of identifying any document or setting forth verbatim its content, you may attach a true and correct copy of the document(s) properly referenced in your answers.

7. Unless defined otherwise in an individual Request for Production, "Identify", "Identity", or "Identification" have the following meanings: (a) as to a person — full name, present or last known residence address, present or last known business address, and residence and business telephone numbers; (b) as to a corporation, governmental entity, partnership, association, or other business entity — full name, present or last known business or operating address, name of its chief executive officer and telephone number; (c) as to a document — (i) title, heading, or caption; (ii) identifying numbers or letters and their significance if necessary to understanding the document and evaluating any claim of protection from discovery; (iii) the date appearing on the document, or if none, the date or approximate date it was prepared; (iv) the number of pages and general nature or description with sufficient particularity to enable precise identification; (v) the name and capacity of the person who signed it, or if unsigned, who prepared it; (vi) the name and capacity of the addressee and of all other persons to whom it or a copy was sent; and (vii) the physical location and custodian(s); (d) as to a statement — (i) the identity of the person who made it, the person who took or recorded it, and all persons present; (ii) the date, location, and method by which it was taken and/or recorded; and (iii) the identity of the person(s) with present or last known possession, custody, or control; (e) as to an incident, occurrence, claim, complaint, notice, or suit — (i) date and place; (ii) what is alleged to have occurred; (iii) a description of the machine, vehicle, or instrument involved; (iv) the identity of the person(s) involved; and (v) for each suit, the style, cause number, court, identity of the plaintiff's attorney, and whether pending or closed; (f) as to a system, procedure, or computer program for reporting, recording, categorizing, organizing, or analyzing {{claims_systems_subject: claims, safety events, or other reported problems or complaints concerning your {{operations_descriptor}}}} — (i) the person(s) responsible; (ii) any internal name, title, number, abbreviation, or acronym; (iii) a detailed description of how it operates; (iv) whether {{affiliates_descriptor}} have access and how such information can be obtained; and (v) whether it compiles periodic reports, summaries, analyses, or digests, and if so their format, internal designation, and the identity of every person with possession, custody, control, or access.

8. If you claim as privileged or otherwise protected from discovery any information or any document responsive to one or more of the following interrogatories or requests, you shall set forth, in detail, all bases for the claim of privilege, and set forth all grounds upon which you rely in claiming that the information or document is privileged or otherwise protected from discovery.

9. If any document which would be responsive to any interrogatory or request for production herein was, but is no longer, in your possession or subject to your control, or is no longer in existence, identify each document, in the manner defined hereinabove, and by additionally stating whether it is missing or lost, it has been destroyed, it has been transferred voluntarily to others, or it has been otherwise disposed of, and in each instance in which it has been destroyed, transferred, or disposed of: (a) explain the circumstances surrounding such disposition; (b) identify the person(s) directing or authorizing its destruction or transfer; (c) the date(s) of such direction or authorization; and (d) whether the document (or copies) are still in existence, and if so, identify the custodian(s) and its (or their) present location(s).

10. "Expert" means any expert who is expected to testify at trial, either in your case in chief or rebuttal, by deposition or live testimony, and any expert who has been informally consulted, retained, or specially employed in anticipation of litigation or preparation for trial, but who will not be called to testify, whose opinions or impressions, including any documents, tangible things, test results, factual observations, data, or work product containing such impressions and opinions, have been reviewed by a testifying expert.

11. "Control" means within your possession, custody, or control and includes constructive possession as long as you, your attorneys, agents, or representatives, whether natural persons or business or legal entities, have superior right to compel the production from any third party, whether natural persons or business or legal entities, and including any agency, authority, or representative.

12+. {{case_specific_definitions: party short names; vehicles or instrumentalities by VIN/serial; corporate-family definitions; regulatory definitions (e.g., FMCSRs); data-system definitions (ELD/ECM/EDR/telematics); pleading-referenced instruments (e.g., a policy raised in the answer); contract definitions (e.g., a lease at issue).}}

## Confer note (bold paragraph, closes the Definition of Terms section)

If you find any of the following discovery requests confusing, unclear, or objectionable in any other way that prevents you from providing a complete answer, please contact me directly at {{attorney_phone}} so that we may discuss the issue. I am open to confer on all matters before court intervention is necessary.

## Notes for reuse

- Definition ¶7(f) in the source exemplar was written for product/warranty cases ("complaints about your products"); adapt the bracketed subject to the defendant's business (drivers/vehicles/operations for a carrier; premises/maintenance for a premises case) or omit when inapplicable.
- The ESI sentence in the preamble and the ESI expansion in ¶4 are additions layered onto the source exemplar for data-heavy cases; omit where unneeded.
- The Verification page that follows the interrogatories section is addressed to the responding defendant (two notary blocks: authorized-representative affidavit and simple sworn form).
